judgment.rationale: The report says a window moved into a FancyZones zone “does not get saved,” but does not explain whether the immediate snap fails or persistence across a new window/restart fails. The generic title and absence of an app/version make the behavior unlocalizable.
evidence: Report lists PowerToys 0.91 and says to open FancyZones, drag a window to a zone, and expect it to stay there.
Actual behavior says the app “does not get saved,” without defining saved state.
No comments, screenshots, or attached logs are present.
judgment.recommended_action: Ask the reporter to identify the persistence step that fails using one named application.

fix_assessment.rationale: The report does not define whether the window fails to snap immediately or its last-zone state fails later; no fix can be selected until the outcome is clarified.

issue_context.summary: A FancyZones window moved into a zone reportedly is “not saved.”
known_information: No application, subsequent relaunch step, or timeline comment is present.
inferences: The wording may refer to last-zone persistence rather than immediate zone operation.
issue_context.analysis: Request one explicit move/close/reopen sequence rather than generic diagnostics.
initial_investigation: Read full issue body and timeline; no comments or linked work.

information_gaps.information: What “the app does not get saved” means: whether it is not remembered as the last zone for a new instance, loses its zone after restart, or does not stay in the zone immediately after dropping it; include application and current version.
information_gaps.why_needed: The title “Test bug” and one-line report do not identify persistence behavior or affected application. FancyZones applies an immediate zone and separately stores last-known placement, so these outcomes require different investigation.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: On current release report one application and exact sequence: move it into a zone, observe immediate position, close/reopen it, and identify when expected state is lost.

comment.body: Could you clarify what “does not get saved” means in one application? After moving a window into a zone, does it fail to stay there immediately, or does it lose the zone only after closing/reopening the app or restarting Windows? Please share the current PowerToys version and the exact step where the expected state disappears.
